title_en: What Can Stand Against a Singly Transmitted Report
body_ar: هل صحيح ما يقال أن النبي (ص) هو الذي شرع رد خبر الآحاد حين لم يعمل بمقتضى ملاحظة ذي اليدين حتى شهد الآخرون بصدق ملاحظته؟ إن هذا لا يقتضي عدم العمل بخبر الآحاد وإنما اقتضى أن خبر ذي اليدين خالفه يقين رسول الله (ص) فهو خبر آحاد عارضه ما هو أقوى منه، فالآحاد أقوى منه خبر رسول الله (ص)، فالرسول (ص) عندما سأله ذو اليدين، قال هل قصرت الصلاة أم نسيت قال كل ذلك لم يكن، فهذا خبر رسول الله (ص) وهو أصدق من ذي اليدين، لكنه تردد بعد هذا فشك وعندما شك اقتضى ذلك أن يسأل لأن خبر ذي اليدين لم يقو على معارضة خبر الرسول (ص) وما كان يتيقنه لكنه شككه فلما حصل عنده الشك طلب المزيد من العلم على القاعدة الشرعية قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنت صادقين، فحصل له العلم بخبر الصحابة.
body_en:
Question: Is it true, as is said, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is the one who established the rejection of the singly transmitted report (ḫabar al-āḥād), when he did not act upon what Dhu al-Yadayn observed until the others testified to the truth of his observation?

Answer: This does not entail not acting upon the singly transmitted report. It entails rather that Dhu al-Yadayn’s report was contradicted by the certainty of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): it was a singly transmitted report opposed by something stronger than it — and stronger than a singly transmitted report is the report of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). For when Dhu al-Yadayn asked the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), saying, "Has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget?", he said, "Neither of these happened." This is the report of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and it is more truthful than Dhu al-Yadayn. But afterwards he wavered and doubted; and when he doubted, that required him to ask — because Dhu al-Yadayn’s report was not strong enough to stand against the report of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and what he held with certainty, yet it made him doubt. When doubt arose in him, he sought further knowledge, in accordance with the Sharia principle {Say: produce your proof, if you are truthful} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:111); and so knowledge came to him through the report of the Companions. [Translator's note: renderings of Qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.]
